context: The most widely accepted model, proposed by the archaeologist **Richard Blanton** (an American scholar who led the Valley of Oaxaca Settlement Pattern Project in the 1970s–80s), is that Monte Albán was a **disembedded capital**: a new political center deliberately placed in neutral territory to unite previously rival communities.

The Mixtec had cleared out the original Zapotec burial, deposited nine new bodies (one primary and eight sacrificial), and filled the chamber with over 500 objects: gold pectorals, gold earrings, gold rings, a gold and turquoise pendant depicting the Mixtec death god, turquoise mosaics, carved jaguar bone with incised genealogical scenes, rock crystal cups, pearl ornaments, and carved jade.
